title: Sarga Nineteen — verses 1–100
html:
Title of the sarga: Śrī-vṛndāvana-yātrā, "The Journey to Sri Vrindavana" (from the colophon: iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye śrī-vṛndāvana-yātrāyām ūnaviṁśaḥ sargaḥ, "Thus [ends] the nineteenth sarga, [in the account of] the journey to Sri Vrindavana, in the great poem Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita"). Metre: - 1–99 — anuṣṭubh (śloka: 8 syllables per pada; in the even padas the fifth to seventh syllables are ⏑—⏑; in the odd padas, besides the normal ⏑——, the permitted variants (vipulā) are used freely). Irregularities of the printed text: in 6 the third pada (paramānanda-purī ca) has ⏑⏑— in the fifth to seventh places, which is neither the normal form nor a vipulā (a licence with a proper name); in 22 the second and third padas of the edition are each a syllable short, and in 25 the second line has 13 syllables instead of 16; in both the text is restored after the Gosvami edition (GGM); in 37 the second pada has seven syllables (nānā nūnanū nanu); in 49 the first pada (avapayo 'tivimalam) has both the second and the third syllables light; 70 has six padas; in 81 the fourth pada has nine syllables (dṛṣṭaye tatra cakāra saḥ). In 45 and 53 (palindromes) each printed line is a single pada. - 100 — mandākrāntā (ma-bha-na-ta-ta-ga-ga: ————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada).

Total verses: 100.

Contents of the passage: the beginning of the journey to Vrindavana (by way of Bengal).
- 1–5 — the decision to go to Mathura by way of the bank of the Ganga:
- 2–3 — an insertion made by the publishers from another edition (footnote);
- Ramananda holds the Lord back; the play on "Vijaya-dashami / the tenth state" (5).
- 6–12 — the companions: Govinda, Jagadananda, Damodara Pandita, Paramananda Puri; mahaprasada for the Vaishnavas of Bengal; on the advice of Puri the sanctified cloth received from Prataparudra is to be sent to the Lord's mother (9–12).
- 13–19 — Damodara is late for the first service; the Lord, "the Ocean of love, out of love", strikes him with a little book (18–19).
- 20–34 — the farewell to Jagannatha and to Puri:
- the Lord sends back those who follow Him, headed by Kashi Mishra (22);
- Ramananda follows Him in a palanquin (26); the loving dispute between them (31–34).
- 35–51 — mahaprasada from Vaninatha; autumn; the Lord embraces the trees as if they were the trees of Vrindavana (43–48); Bhuvaneshvara.
- 52–80 — a village with a house built by Ramananda; Kataka (Cuttack): the temple of Gopinatha; the brahmana Svapneshvara; a garden with a bakula tree.
- 81–92 — Prataparudra comes with an army of four divisions (drawn up in rings, 87–88) and falls at the Lord's feet.
- 93–100 — the king orders Mangaraja and Harichandana to escort the Lord beyond the Mahanadi and to raise memorial pillars; the night's halt at Chaturdvara.

Verse 1

द्रुतचामीकराकारो मथुरां चलितुं ततः ।
लसत्करिकराकारोद्दामदोर्द्वितयो बभौ ॥१॥

druta-cāmīkarākāro mathurāṁ calituṁ tataḥ |
lasat-kari-karākāroddāma-dor-dvitayo babhau ||1||

druta — of molten; cāmīkara — gold; ākāraḥ — [whose] form [was like]; mathurām — to Mathura; calitum — to go; tataḥ — then; lasat — of a shining; kari — elephant; kara — the trunk; ākāra — [like] in form; uddāma — mighty; doḥ — of arms; dvitayaḥ — [whose] pair [was]; babhau — shone.

1Then [the Lord], His form like molten gold, His two mighty arms like the trunk of a shining elephant, shone, [setting out] to go to Mathura.

Note. The metre of the sarga is anuṣṭubh (except where otherwise stated).

Verse 2–3

{ प्रयातुं यमुनातीरं गङ्गातीरे मनो दधे ।
यत्तटे सोऽवतीर्णोऽस्ति तस्यां प्रीतिर्महीयसी ॥२॥
दक्षिणादागतो यावत्तावत्तत्र महाप्रभुः ।
मथुरायां चलत्येव रामानन्दोऽत्र बाधते ॥३॥ }

prayātuṁ yamunā-tīraṁ gaṅgā-tīre mano dadhe |
yat-taṭe so 'vatīrṇo 'sti tasyāṁ prītir mahīyasī ||2||
dakṣiṇād āgato yāvat tāvat tatra mahāprabhuḥ |
mathurāyāṁ calaty eva rāmānando 'tra bādhate ||3||

prayātum — to set out; yamunā — of the Yamuna; tīram — for the bank; gaṅgā — of the Ganga; tīre — on the bank; manaḥ — [His] mind; dadhe — He set; yat — on whose; taṭe — bank; saḥ — He; avatīrṇaḥ asti — has descended; tasyām — for her; prītiḥ — love; mahīyasī — very great.

dakṣiṇāt — from the south; āgataḥ — returned; yāvat … tāvat — no sooner … than; tatra — then; mahāprabhuḥ — Mahaprabhu; mathurāyām — for Mathura; calati eva — is already setting off; rāmānandaḥ — Ramananda; atra — at this; bādhate — hinders (holds [Him] back).

2–3Wishing to set out for the bank of the Yamuna, He set His mind [first] on the bank of the Ganga: for it is on her bank that He has descended, and His love for her is very great. No sooner had Mahaprabhu returned from the south than He was already setting off for Mathura — but at this Ramananda holds Him back.

Note. The edition's footnote (in Sanskrit): "In this book two verses were illegible because of a printing defect; therefore, after consulting another book, they were typeset by computer." Verses 2–3 are enclosed in braces; that is, we have a later reprint with an insertion. Bādhate means rather "holds back"; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.4–8, 85–92: for years Sarvabhauma and Ramananda dissuade the Lord from going to Vrindavana, until He reproaches them.

Verse 4

चातुर्मास्यान्तरे नाथं कर्हिचिद्गमनोद्यतम् ।
उवाच बहुदुःखेन श्रीरामानन्दरायकः ॥४॥

cāturmāsyāntare nāthaṁ karhicid gamanodyatam |
uvāca bahu-duḥkhena śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ ||4||

cāturmāsya — of the Chaturmasya; antare — at the end; nātham — to the Master; karhicit — once; gamana — to depart; udyatam — ready; uvāca — said; bahu — with great; duḥkhena — sorrow; śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ — Sri Ramananda Raya.

4Once, at the end of the Chaturmasya, when the Master was ready to depart, Sri Ramananda Raya said with great sorrow:

Verse 5

दशम्यां विजयायां तु गमनं भविता प्रभोः ।
दशम्यां विजयायां तु दशायामहमग्रतः ॥५॥

daśamyāṁ vijayāyāṁ tu gamanaṁ bhavitā prabhoḥ |
daśamyāṁ vijayāyāṁ tu daśāyām aham agrataḥ ||5||

daśamyām — on the tenth [day]; vijayāyām — of Vijaya; tu — indeed; gamanam — the departure; bhavitā — will take place; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; daśamyām — in the tenth; vijayāyām — all-conquering; tu — but; daśāyām — in the state; aham — I [shall be]; agrataḥ — before [that].

5"On Vijaya-dashami the Lord's departure will take place — but I shall be in the tenth, all-conquering state before [that]."

Note. A play on words (yamaka: the first half of each line is the same), explained in the edition's Sanskrit commentary: vijayā daśamī is the festival of Vijaya-dashami (in autumn); in the second line vijayā is "she who conquers especially" (viśeṣeṇa jayatīti), and daśamī daśā is the tenth of the ten states of one in love, that is, the end of life. The commentary gives the list: "attraction of the eyes, attachment of the mind, constant thought, sleeplessness, emaciation, aversion to [other] objects, loss of shame, madness, swooning, dying — these are the states in order." The sense: "The Lord will depart on the day of Vijaya, but I shall die even before."

Verse 6

गोविन्दो जगदानन्दः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः ।
परमानन्दपुरी च तत्सङ्गे मिलिता ययुः ॥६॥

govindo jagadānandaḥ śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ |
paramānanda-purī ca tat-saṅge militā yayuḥ ||6||

govindaḥ — Govinda; jagadānandaḥ — Jagadananda; śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ — Sri Damodara Pandita; paramānanda-purī — Paramananda Puri; ca — and; tat-saṅge — in His company; militāḥ — together; yayuḥ — went.

6Govinda, Jagadananda, Sri Damodara Pandita and Paramananda Puri went together in His company.

Note. In the third pada (paramānanda-purī ca: ⏑⏑——⏑⏑—⏑) the fifth to seventh syllables are ⏑⏑—, which is neither the normal form of the odd pada of the anuṣṭubh (⏑——) nor one of its permitted variants (vipulā); a licence with a proper name.

Verse 7

गङ्गातीरे समागत्य वैष्णवेभ्यो विसर्जितुम् ।
महाप्रसादान् विविधान्नेतुं तत्रादिशत् प्रभुः ॥७॥

gaṅgā-tīre samāgatya vaiṣṇavebhyo visarjitum |
mahāprasādān vividhān netuṁ tatrādiśat prabhuḥ ||7||

gaṅgā — of the Ganga; tīre — on the bank; samāgatya — having arrived; vaiṣṇavebhyaḥ — to the Vaishnavas; visarjitum — to distribute; mahā-prasādān — mahaprasada; vividhān — of various kinds; netum — to take along; tatra — then; ādiśat — ordered; prabhuḥ — the Lord.

7Then the Lord ordered that mahaprasada of various kinds be taken along, to distribute it to the Vaishnavas on arriving at the bank of the Ganga.

Verse 8

एते नाथनिदेशेन मुदिता भूय आददुः ।
महाप्रसादान् विपुलान् डोरचन्दनमुख्यकान् ॥८॥

ete nātha-nideśena muditā bhūya ādaduḥ |
mahāprasādān vipulān ḍora-candana-mukhyakān ||8||

ete — they; nātha — of the Master; nideśena — by the order; muditāḥ — joyful; bhūyaḥ — much; ādaduḥ — took; mahā-prasādān — mahaprasada; vipulān — abundant; ḍora — cords; candana — sandalwood paste; mukhyakān — and so on (lit. headed by).

8At the Master's order they joyfully took much abundant mahaprasada — cords, sandalwood paste and so on.

Note. Ḍora — the sanctified silk cords of Jagannatha (paṭṭa-ḍorī).

Verse 9

मात्रे निर्म्माल्यवसनमात्मेच्छाभिर्महाप्रभुः ।
परमानन्दपुर्यूढां परमां युक्तिमादधे ॥९॥

mātre nirmālya-vasanam ātmecchābhir mahāprabhuḥ |
paramānanda-puryūḍhāṁ paramāṁ yuktim ādadhe ||9||

mātre — for [His] mother; nirmālya — sanctified; vasanam — a garment; ātma — by [His] own; icchābhiḥ — wishes; mahāprabhuḥ — Mahaprabhu; paramānanda-purī — by Paramananda Puri; ūḍhām — put forward; paramām — excellent; yuktim — counsel; ādadhe — adopted.

9[Wishing to give] His mother, of His own accord, a sanctified garment, Mahaprabhu adopted the excellent counsel put forward by Paramananda Puri.

Note. The counsel itself is given in 12.

Verse 10

इदं श्रीमज्जगन्नाथनिर्म्माल्यं परमांशुकम् ।
प्रतापरुद्रेण च मे दत्तं परमदुर्लभम् ॥१०॥

idaṁ śrīmaj-jagannātha-nirmālyaṁ paramāṁśukam |
pratāparudreṇa ca me dattaṁ parama-durlabham ||10||

idam — this; śrīmat-jagannātha — of Sriman Jagannatha; nirmālyam — the sanctified [remnant]; parama — excellent; aṁśukam — cloth; pratāparudreṇa — by Prataparudra; ca — and; me — to Me; dattam — given; parama — extremely; durlabham — rare.

10"This excellent cloth, the sanctified [remnant] of Sriman Jagannatha, extremely rare, was given to Me by Prataparudra.

Verse 11

कस्मै दास्यामि तन्नूनं गदितुं त्वमिहार्हसि ।
मया सन्दिग्धमनसा स्थीयते साम्प्रतं खलु ॥११॥

kasmai dāsyāmi tan nūnaṁ gadituṁ tvam ihārhasi |
mayā sandigdha-manasā sthīyate sāmprataṁ khalu ||11||

kasmai — to whom; dāsyāmi — shall I give; tat — it; nūnam — then; gaditum — to say; tvam — you; iha — here; arhasi — ought; mayā — by Me; sandigdha — doubting; manasā — with a mind; sthīyate — it is remained (I remain); sāmpratam — now; khalu — indeed.

11To whom shall I give it? You ought to tell Me this here, for I am now indeed in doubt."

Verse 12

इत्युक्तोऽसौ पुरीस्वामी बभाषेऽथ महाप्रभुम् ।
जनन्यै देयमेतत्तु ममैतन्मतमुत्तमम् ॥१२॥

ity ukto 'sau purī-svāmī babhāṣe 'tha mahāprabhum |
jananyai deyam etat tu mamaitan matam uttamam ||12||

iti — thus; uktaḥ — addressed; asau — this; purī-svāmī — Puri Svami; babhāṣe — said; atha — then; mahāprabhum — to Mahaprabhu; jananyai — to [Your] mother; deyam — should be given; etat tu — this; mama — my; etat — this [is]; matam — opinion; uttamam — firm (lit. highest).

12Thus addressed, Puri Svami then said to Mahaprabhu: "This should be given to [Your] mother — that is my firm opinion."

Note. Puri Svami is Paramananda Puri (cf. 9).

Verse 13

ऊचे पूर्वेद्युरसकौ रसकौतुकविभ्रमः ।
विभ्रमच्छेदकृद्दृष्टिर्हृद्दृष्टिसुखदः प्रभुः ॥१३॥

ūce pūrvedyur asakau rasa-kautuka-vibhramaḥ |
vibhrama-ccheda-kṛd-dṛṣṭir hṛd-dṛṣṭi-sukhadaḥ prabhuḥ ||13||

ūce — said; pūrvedyuḥ — on the day before; asakau — this; rasa — in rasa; kautuka — of delight; vibhramaḥ — [whose] charm [is]; vibhrama — of delusion; cheda — the cutting; kṛt — effecting; dṛṣṭiḥ — [whose] glance [is]; hṛt — to the heart; dṛṣṭi — [and] to the eyes; sukha-daḥ — giving joy; prabhuḥ — the Lord.

13On the day before [the departure] this Lord — full of the charm of delight in rasa, whose glance cuts away delusion, who gives joy to the heart and the eyes — said:

Note. A chain of repetitions at the junctions (rasakau / rasa-kautuka, vibhramaḥ / vibhrama-, dṛṣṭiḥ / hṛd-dṛṣṭi-). Asakau is a by-form of asau with the suffix -ak-, chosen here for the sound-play.

Verse 14

गायं गायं गमिष्यामि जगन्नाथं विलोकितुम् ।
दामोदरोऽसौ मत्सङ्गे गायन् स्थास्यति निश्चितम् ॥१४॥

gāyaṁ gāyaṁ gamiṣyāmi jagannāthaṁ vilokitum |
dāmodaro 'sau mat-saṅge gāyan sthāsyati niścitam ||14||

gāyam gāyam — singing and singing; gamiṣyāmi — I shall go; jagannātham — Jagannatha; vilokitum — to see; dāmodaraḥ — Damodara; asau — this; mat-saṅge — with Me; gāyan — singing; sthāsyati — will be; niścitam — certainly.

14"I shall go to see Jagannatha, singing all the way, and this Damodara will certainly be [there] with Me, singing."

Note. In verses 6 and 24 the Lord's companion in this episode is expressly called Damodara Pandita, so presumably it is he here too, although the one who usually sings for the Lord is Svarupa Damodara. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 15

इत्यसौ रजनीशेषे प्रथमावसरं विभोः ।
निजकीर्त्तनसंहर्षैर्गच्छन् पथि बभौ प्रभुः ॥१५॥

ity asau rajanī-śeṣe prathamāvasaraṁ vibhoḥ |
nija-kīrttana-saṁharṣair gacchan pathi babhau prabhuḥ ||15||

iti — thus [having spoken]; asau — He; rajanī — of the night; śeṣe — at the end; prathama — to the first; avasaram — service; vibhoḥ — of the All-pervading Lord; nija — of His own; kīrttana — kirtana; saṁharṣaiḥ — with the raptures; gacchan — going; pathi — on the road; babhau — shone; prabhuḥ — the Lord.

15Having spoken thus, at the end of the night the Lord, going along the road to the first service (avasara) of the All-pervading Lord [Jagannatha], shone with the raptures of His own kirtana.

Verse 16

दैवाद्दामोदरः सोऽयं मिलितो नाभवत्तदा ।
सिंहद्वारे क्षणं तस्थौ तमपेक्ष्य स्वयं प्रभुः ॥१६॥

daivād dāmodaraḥ so 'yaṁ milito nābhavat tadā |
siṁha-dvāre kṣaṇaṁ tasthau tam apekṣya svayaṁ prabhuḥ ||16||

daivāt — as fate would have it; dāmodaraḥ — Damodara; saḥ ayam — that very; militaḥ — joined; na abhavat — had not; tadā — then; siṁha-dvāre — at the Lion Gate; kṣaṇam — for a while; tasthau — stood; tam — for him; apekṣya — waiting; svayam — Himself; prabhuḥ — the Lord.

16As fate would have it, that Damodara had not joined [them] then, and the Lord Himself stood for a while at the Lion Gate, waiting for him.

Verse 17

भावाभावाभिभावाभिभवभावे बभौ भवः ।
विभावेवम्भावभावे बभूव भुवि वैभवम् ॥१७॥
(द्व्यक्षरः)

bhāvābhāvābhibhāvābhibhava-bhāve babhau bhavaḥ |
vibhāv evam-bhāva-bhāve babhūva bhuvi vaibhavam ||17||
(dvyakṣaraḥ)

(following the word division of the edition's commentary: bhāva abhāva abhibhāva abhibhava bhāve babhau bhavaḥ | vibhau evambhāva bhāve babhūva bhuvi vaibhavam): bhāva — of the presence; abhāva — from the absence; abhibhāva — [by] the all-pervading state [of separation]; abhibhava — of being overcome; bhāve — [when there was] the state; babhau — shone forth; bhavaḥ — the birth [of Damodara]; vibhau — [when] the Master [was]; evam-bhāva — such; bhāve — in a state; babhūva — there arose; bhuvi — on earth; vaibhavam — glory.

17When [the Lord] was in the state of being overcome by the all-pervading state [of separation] arising from the absence [of Damodara], the birth [of Damodara] shone forth; when the Master was in such a state, [his] glory arose on earth.

Note. Dvyakṣara, a "two-consonant" verse: the whole verse uses only the consonants bh and v (a kind of citra-kāvya). The translation follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary: "bhāva is existence; its abhāva is the absence of Sri Damodara; abhi-bhāva is the state of separation on all sides; abhibhava is being overcome by it; in this state bhavaḥ, the birth [of Damodara], shone forth, and on earth there was vaibhavam, honour. The sense: he in separation from whom the Lord becomes agitated — his birth is fruitful, and honour is his." The commentary adds: "From here on there follows one verse each on one, two, three and more consonants."

Verse 18

ततः किञ्चिद्विलम्बेन मिलितोऽभूत् स भूसुरः ।
प्रभुराविष्टचित्तोऽसौ तं दृष्ट्वा कुपितोऽभवत् ॥१८॥

tataḥ kiñcid vilambena milito 'bhūt sa bhūsuraḥ |
prabhur āviṣṭa-citto 'sau taṁ dṛṣṭvā kupito 'bhavat ||18||

tataḥ — then; kiñcit — with a slight; vilambena — delay; militaḥ abhūt — joined [them]; saḥ — that; bhūsuraḥ — brahmana (lit. god on earth); prabhuḥ — the Lord; āviṣṭa — absorbed [in feeling]; cittaḥ — [whose] heart [was]; asau — He; tam — him; dṛṣṭvā — seeing; kupitaḥ — angry; abhavat — became.

18Then, after a slight delay, that brahmana joined [them]; the Lord, His heart absorbed [in feeling], became angry on seeing him.

Note. The Lord's "anger" (kupita) here is a play of love with His eternal associate, not a worldly emotion: the Lord is not subject to anger, and Karnapura himself names the cause in verse 19 — "out of love" (praṇayāt).

Verse 19

तं तु गीतापुस्तिकया पृष्ठे भूयो जघान सः ।
निष्पिपेष पदाघातैः प्रणयात् प्रणयाम्बुधिः ॥१९॥

taṁ tu gītā-pustikayā pṛṣṭhe bhūyo jaghāna saḥ |
niṣpipeṣa padāghātaiḥ praṇayāt praṇayāmbudhiḥ ||19||

tam tu — him; gītā — of songs (?); pustikayā — with a little book; pṛṣṭhe — on the back; bhūyaḥ — many times; jaghāna — struck; saḥ — He; niṣpipeṣa — pummelled; pada — of the feet; āghātaiḥ — with blows; praṇayāt — out of love; praṇaya — of love; ambudhiḥ — the Ocean.

19And He, the Ocean of love, out of love struck him many times on the back with a little book of songs and pummelled him with kicks.

Note. Gītā-pustikā is either "a little book of the Gita" or "a little book of songs". There is no such episode in the Chaitanya-charitamrita. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 20

इत्थं प्रविश्य प्रासादं दृष्ट्वा श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
नत्वा स्तुत्वा च चलितुं मनश्चक्रे कृपानिधिः ॥२०॥

नलाल ललनालीनां लीलां लाननिलो ललन् ॥४१॥
(द्व्यक्षरः)

līlā-lolāli-lalanā lalan nalina-lālanaiḥ |
nalāla (? calāla) lalanālīnāṁ līlāṁ lān anilo lalan ||41||
(dvyakṣaraḥ)

(following the edition's commentary): līlā — in play; lola — restless; ali — of the bees; lalanāḥ — the female companions; lalan — desiring; nalina — of the lotuses; lālanaiḥ — by the swaying; lalanā-ālīnām — of those clinging to [their] companions; līlām — the play; lān — taking; anilaḥ — the wind; lalan — desiring [= well pleased]; nalāla (?) — moved.

41The wind, swaying the lotuses, desiring the female companions of the bees, restless in their play, and taking on the play proper to those who cling to their companions, moved along, well pleased (?).

Note. A dvyakṣara: the verse uses only two consonants, l and n. The commentary: "anilaḥ — the wind; nalina-lālanaiḥ — by swaying the lotuses: as a husband beckons his playful wife with his hand, so the wind, desiring the bees' companions, moved, swaying the lotuses, [its] hands." The commentary explains the verb nalāla as cacāla, "moved", by the rule that ḍa and la are identical (from the root laḍ); the passage is obscure (?). The conjecture calāla recorded in the IAST line would break the two-consonant scheme. Metre: both lines are regular (the first pada is a na-vipulā). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

(निरोष्ठ्यः)
